title: Applied ML Evals: Unified Onboarding & Regression Playbook
author: Priya Shah
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates applied ML evals best-practices spanning eval harness setup, prompt set standards, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and a regression triage runbook. It is intended for ML Engineers, SREs, and platform integrators who onboard models to Redwood’s inference platform or own regression investigations.

Scope:
- Eval harness configuration for model onboarding and periodic checks.
- Standardized prompt sets and benchmark definitions for functional and safety checks.
- Quantization profile recommendations and compatibility matrix.
- Quality guardrails and acceptance criteria for production rollouts.
- Regression triage process (alerts -> investigate -> remediate -> postmortem).

Owners and Roles:
- Playbook owner: Priya Shah (Applied ML)
- Primary reviewers: Carlos Mendez (Runtime), Aiko Tanaka (SRE)
- Onboarding owner per model: assigned in model registry (Model Owner alias)
- Incident lead for regressions: oncall-applied-ml rotation

Guiding Principles:
1. Reproducible evaluations: all eval runs must be captured in the eval-harness with commit-linked configs and deterministic seeds where applicable.
2. Signal-first: guardrails focus on clear, measurable signals (SLOs, metric deltas, token-level quality checks).
3. Fast triage: provide a repeatable path enabling a one-hour initial diagnosis and a two-day remediation plan for regressions.

1) Eval Harness Configuration
- Recommended service: eval-harness (internal repo: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness).
- Required artifacts per run: model binary identifier (model_id:version), config.yaml, prompt-set id, dataset snapshot id, seed, runtime profile (hw type + quantization).
- Minimum metrics to capture (per-run):
  - avg_latency_ms (95th percentile),
  - tokens_per_second,
  - perplexity (if applicable),
  - BLEU/ROUGE/EM/F1 per task (task-dependent),
  - safety flag rate (disallowed/high-risk outputs),
  - semantic-similarity to reference (embedding cosine).
- Example eval command:
  ```bash
  ./run_eval.sh --model-id rl-model-7b:v2 --prompt-set finance-qna-v1 --dataset snapshots/2026-11-01.tgz --profile fp16-cuda --out results/rl-model-7b-v2-finance-20261101.json
  ```
- CI gating: onboarding PRs must run the harness with the baseline model and a smoke prompt-set; failure blocks merge.

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks
- Prompt set taxonomy:
  - smoke: 20 examples to catch obvious failures.
  - functional: 200–1,000 examples covering product-specific flows.
  - benchmark: 1k–10k examples sampled from representative traffic for throughput/quality regression detection.
  - adversarial/safety: curated cases to surface policy violations.
- Prompt naming convention: <domain>-<purpose>-v<major> (e.g., customer-support-functional-v1).
- Metadata required for each prompt set (stored in catalog): id, owner, domain, coverage_tags, creation_date, last_reviewed, dataset_snapshot_id, expected_metric_thresholds.
- Example prompt-set entry (text format in catalog):
  | id | owner | domain | size | primary_metrics | notes |
  | customer-support-functional-v1 | product-nli | support | 450 | EM/F1, response_length, safety_flag_rate | uses anonymized user logs|

3) Model Onboarding Checklist (minimum gating)
- Pre-onboard: security review, sensitive-data scan, and licensing check.
- Eval requirements:
  1. Run smoke + functional prompt-sets against current production baseline and new model.
  2. Provide a delta report with per-metric % change and significance test (bootstrap or paired t-test where applicable).
  3. Confirm throughput/cost profile: tokens/sec and estimated $/M tokens at target deployment profile (batching, kv-cache hit rate).
  4. Verify quantization compatibility: test fp16, int8 (where supported) with representative prompt lengths.
- Acceptance criteria (default, unless product-specific thresholds set):
  - No >3% regression in primary quality metric for functional prompts without compensating latency/cost improvements.
  - Safety flag rate <= baseline + 0.1%.
  - P95 latency within SLA (e.g., p95 <= 200ms for interactive-tier deployments) or documented tradeoffs for lower latency with dedicated capacity.
- Rollout plan: canary (5% traffic, 24h), ramp (25%, 48h), full (100%) with automatic rollback on predefined triggers.

4) Quality Guardrails
- Guardrail categories and examples:
  - Accuracy regressions: primary metric delta thresholds (e.g., EM/F1, BLEU).
  - Safety/policy violations: any increase in policy-violation rate above 0.1% absolute raises immediate triage.
  - Latency/cost regressions: token cost or latency increase > 15% requires assessment.
  - Stability: high variance in outputs for same seed/input flagged as instability.
- Monitoring signals to track in Redwood Console dashboards: per-route quality metrics, token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latencies, kv-cache hit rate, safety flags.
- Automated alerting rules (examples):
  - Quality-drop: if primary_metric_drop > 2.5% relative to baseline for 30m
  - Safety-spike: safety_flag_rate > baseline + 0.5% for 10m
  - Latency-spike: p95_latency > SLA_threshold for 15m

5) Quantization Profiles and Compatibility
- Profiles supported (nomenclature used in artifact registry):
  - fp16-cuda: standard mixed-precision on CUDA devices (recommended for most models).
  - int8-static: static 8-bit quantization with calibration dataset (recommended for non-sensitive, high-throughput workloads).
  - int8-dynamic: dynamic per-batch quantization (lower quality risk, faster evaluation cycles).
  - bf16-tpu: bf16 for TPUs where available.
- Quantization testing matrix (minimum):
  | model_size | fp16 | int8-static | int8-dynamic | notes |
  | 3B | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | int8-static reduces mem by ~2.5x with ~1–2% quality delta |
  | 7B | ✓ | ✓ (calibrate) | ✓ | calibration set should contain target-domain prompts |
  | 70B | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | int8-static often unstable; prefer mixed-fp16 or dynamic |
- Calibration guidance: use 2–5k representative prompts (from functional prompt-sets) isolated to avoid PII leakage; store calibration snapshots in dataset storage.
- Validation: run full functional eval on quantized binary and compare against fp16 baseline; record metric deltas and latency/cost improvements.

6) Regression Triage Playbook (step-by-step)
- Trigger sources: CI eval failures, production alerts, customer reports, manual review.
- Initial 1-hour triage (owner: oncall-applied-ml):
  1. Gather context: model_id, model_version, deployment_profile, recent rollouts, alerts (links), eval results.
  2. Reproduce: run smoke prompt-set locally against production model and newly-deployed model (if available).
  3. Classify regression: quality, safety, latency, or cost.
  4. Check recent changes: PRs, dependency updates (tokenizer, runtime kernels), quantization changes, routing policies.
  5. If safety-related: escalate immediately to Security & Trust and open incident channel.
- Detailed investigation (next 24–48 hours):
  - Compare model outputs using diff tools (token-level and semantic similarity).
  - Run pairwise evals (baseline vs current) across functional and benchmark prompt-sets and produce a delta matrix.
  - Validate runtime stack: kernel changes, CUDA/cuDNN driver versions, runtime flags (continuous batching settings, kv-cache handling).
- Short-term mitigations:
  - Roll back to last known-good model/version.
  - Temporarily route to fallback model variant (lower-cost or lower-latency variant with better baseline).
  - Apply server-side filters/corrections for specific failure modes (if safe to do so).
- Long-term remediation: root-cause analysis, bug fix or model retraining, updated guardrails/prompt-sets, and improved CI gating.
- Postmortem: document timeline, root cause, actions taken, owners, and preventive measures. Postmortems live under /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems and must be linked in related_pages.

7) Runbooks and Templates
- Immediate-reproduce runbook (copyable):
  1. Checkout eval-harness at commit linked in deployment.
  2. Run: ./run_eval.sh --model-id <model> --prompt-set smoke --profile <profile> --out /tmp/regression.json
  3. Diff outputs: python tools/diff_outputs.py --baseline baseline.json --current /tmp/regression.json --metrics
  4. If delta > threshold, open ticket in JIRA with summary, reproduction artifacts, and initial hypothesis.
- Release checklist template (for model owners):
  - [ ] Security scan complete
  - [ ] Licensing & weights approved
  - [ ] Eval harness: smoke & functional runs completed
  - [ ] Quantization validation completed
  - [ ] Performance/cost estimates documented
  - [ ] Rollout plan and rollback criteria defined

Appendix: Example Delta Report Fields (CSV-friendly)
- model_id,model_version,prompt_set,metric_name,baseline_value,current_value,absolute_delta,relative_delta,significance_pvalue,notes
